purpose: Section 25.2: v2_stage1_scoring.py must not be treated as execution-ready until subprocess isolation is built AND its own control demonstrates the same bound e2a_instrument_diagnostic.py already demonstrated (that instrument's DINST_HOSTILE_REVIEW.md measured a real 44.4 GB / 95 s pathological case). This is that control, run against the real (unmocked) canonicalise_isolated().
disclosed_scope_difference: This control does NOT reproduce a naturally-occurring pathological expression at the frozen 23.5 GiB scoring-tier-2 ceiling -- no such case was found in a practical search budget (three expansion/nested-trig candidates were tried and either completed quickly or were CPU-slow without demonstrated memory pressure; not committed, not claimed as evidence). Instead it demonstrates the SAME safety property -- real resource exhaustion, correctly contained and typed as UNRESOLVED, never silently OK, never crashing the caller -- by lowering RLIMIT_AS to a level a REAL sympy/numpy import cannot fit in, which is real memory pressure on a real subprocess, not a mock. This is a narrower-scope control than e2a's and is disclosed as such rather than presented as equivalent.

normal_at_frozen_ceiling.note: demonstrates normal operation is unaffected by the isolation layer

induced_resource_pressure.note: a real subprocess died from real memory pressure during sympy/numpy import -- an uncaught SystemError inside CPython's own import machinery, NOT one of canonicalise()'s own typed MemoryError/RecursionError catches -- and the OUTER subprocess-isolation layer still correctly contained it and returned UNRESOLVED, never propagating to crash the caller and never becoming a scientific label. This is the exact property this control exists to demonstrate: the isolation boundary does not depend on the inner failure being a type canonicalise() itself anticipated.
